item.title: Un-Fired Sgt. Retires
item.description: A police sergeant who was fired for allegedly lying about a traffic stop-turned-civilian complaint -- and who then got her job back when her termination was overturned by a state arbitration panel -- has retired. Her retirement comes a few weeks after the police commission turned down the chief's recommendation that she be promoted to lieutenant. The post Un-Fired Sgt. Retires appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Housing Authority To Rehab Crawford Manor
item.description: The city's housing authority is moving forward with a "substantial rehabilitation" of George Crawford Manor, a 109-unit high-rise building for senior and disabled tenants, in order to modernize the building and boost accessibility and energy efficiency. The post Housing Authority To Rehab Crawford Manor appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: 30 Years Later, Tragedy Fuels Rap Artist’s Debut Single
item.description: It was an April day in 1995. Two boys, each 5, were playing tag with a group of kids near C-Town Supermarket in Fair Haven. One slipped through the locked gate of a power station that controlled all the streetlights. He climbed onto the transformer. The 13,800-volt shock that went through him was fatal. The post 30 Years Later, Tragedy Fuels Rap Artist’s Debut Single appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: “A Huge Step Towards Change, Hopefully A Positive One”
item.description: Jose Lara got a call from his son in Caracas at 1 a.m. Saturday about how helicopters were flying above the Venezuelan capital. Roughly 17 hours later, he and two dozen fellow Venezuelan émigrés gathered outside City Hall to celebrate a U.S. military action that they hope spells the end of the Maduro regime. The post “A Huge Step Towards Change, Hopefully A Positive One” appeared first on New Haven Independent.
